  3. Crash reports and the symbols of a build

#Crash reports and the symbols of a build

When Wren crashes, src/crashtrace writes <profile>\crashes\crash <date> <time>.txt (the faulting thread's stack) and a minidump beside it (.dmp). A program that ended itself with its session open (ExitProcess or TerminateProcess, whoever called them in the executable) leaves exit <date>.txt with the stack that asked for it. A session that ended with no chance to write one is reported at the next start as unclean exit <date>.txt, which says what is left to know: Windows' Application Error event of that process (a fail-fast), a restart of the machine, or a kill from outside. A crash that wrote its report leaves none, nor does a close ended by the shutdown watchdog (shutdown.log in the profile says what it waited for).

What is written and when, for a report to survive what caused it:

  • A stack overflow is handled on the thread that overflowed, so each thread keeps room for the handler. The main thread asks for it in crashtrace. Each thread of host.thread_start asks for it at its start (src/host/thread_<os>.odin): a stack guarantee of 64 KiB on Windows, an alternate signal stack on Linux. Without it, Windows dispatched the overflow on one page and the process could end with no report; Linux killed it at once. A thread of core:thread or of a library has no such room.
  • Every faulting thread waits for the report. A second fault (the threads of a pass reading the same freed block) used to end the process under the writer.
  • The filter runs only if the system's search for a handler walks the stack to the thread's start. On a stack it cannot follow (a return address written over, a jump through a bad pointer) it gives up and ends the process with no handler called. The vectored handler walks the stack the same way first, for every 0xC... code, and reports when the walk stops short.
  • The stack is walked in a copy (crashtrace.Stack_Copy): the walk of a damaged stack ends, it does not fault. The report's thread falling on something else ends that thread; what it wrote stays.
  • The text comes first, addresses before names, the session file goes as soon as the cause is written, and the minidump comes last: DbgHelp allocates and takes locks that the crash may have left held.

#What a report says

Wren 0.4.0 (g6933902 2026-10-26)

*** crash: exception (0xC000008C) at 0x7FF8A66B408A, thread 40736
  build wren.exe 6ADF67692DFE000, base 0x7FF741D90000, size 0x2DFE000
  #00 0x7FF8A66B408A RaiseException+0x8A  [KERNELBASE.dll+0xC408A]
  #01 0x7FF741D98491 ?+0x0  [wren.exe+0x8491]
  ...
  • build <exe> <fingerprint>: the build that crashed. The fingerprint is the link time stamp and the image size of the exe's PE header (%08X%X, the key a symbol server uses for an executable): every link makes a new one, and signing does not change it. base is where the exe was loaded.
  • Each frame: its address, what DbgHelp found in the process, and [module+offset]. A development, debug, check or profile build has its PDB beside it: the frames have names, files and lines. A release has no PDB (-debug would change the program: ODIN_DEBUG, the Direct3D debug layer, other code), so its own frames say ? or the nearest export, which is wrong; the offsets are what counts.
  • reading address 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF: not -1. The system gives that for any address that is not canonical: the bytes of something else read as a pointer, most often a record freed and written over. The report adds (not canonical), and in a build with freed memory poisoned a pointer read from freed memory (testing).

#The symbols of a build

build.bat links every variant with /MAP (it changes nothing in the exe: the sections are byte for byte the same) and wrentool symbols -Publish renames the map build\<exe>-<fingerprint>.map; a release's is also kept in build\symbols (the 20 latest). The map lists every function with its address: Odin names a procedure pkg::proc, and a private one pkg::[file.odin]::proc, so a frame gets its function and, often, its file; there are no line numbers (those need the debug information of -debug).

The map is never in what a user gets: wrentool package puts it in build\dist\symbols\<package>-<fingerprint>.map, the CI keeps it as an artifact (wren-symbols-<commit>; wren-<version>-symbols for a release, 90 days), and wrentool experimental leaves it beside the zip (and zipped in the -Vault folder).

#Naming the frames of a report

build\wrentool crash-symbolize "<profile>\crashes\crash 2026-10-26 15-47-09.txt" [-Symbols <folder or .map>] [-Exe <exe with its PDB>]

It reads the build line, finds *-<fingerprint>.map (in -Symbols, the report's folder, build\, build\symbols) and rewrites each frame inside the program as function+0xoffset (file.odin) [exe+0xoffset]. A report from before the build line has only addresses: the minidump beside it gives the base and the fingerprint (its module list). Given a .dmp alone it names the exception's address. -Symbols <file.map> takes a map of another link, for instance the same commit rebuilt with the same flags: the tool warns that the time stamps differ, and the Odin frames are right as long as the code is the same. -Exe uses an exe and its PDB through DbgHelp instead (files and lines; a development build).

The crash of 26/10 (an experimental build without the build line), named from its minidump and a rebuild of 6933902 with the same flags:

  #01 ... runtime.windows_trap_array_bounds+0x21  (procs_windows_amd64.odin)  [...exe+0x8491]
  #02 ... runtime.bounds_trap+0x9
  #03 ... runtime.bounds_check_error.handle_error-720+0x68
  #04 ... ui.spacer+0x316
  #05 ... browser.build_ui+0x3A8D
  #06 ... browser.frame+0x7D12
  #07 ... browser.main+0x15575

#Tests

src\tools\e2e\crash_reports.odin (in test_all) makes src/tools/crashmodes die in each way and looks at what is left. The @(test) of src/tools/wrentool/deps/symbols_test.odin builds it as a release is built (no PDB, a map), makes it index out of range, and checks that the report has the build line and module offsets, that wrentool crash-symbolize names crashmodes.index_out_of_range under main, and that a report without the build line is named through its minidump. src/crashtrace has a unit test of the fingerprint (read in memory and from the file).
